list.heading: Knowledge
list.description: The knowledge packs the connected Core reports. The list is served and paginated by the Core; this surface shows only what the Core returns and invents no packs, counts, or totals. A digest is a content-identity value only — never safety, authenticity, or factual truth.
list.emptyAll: No knowledge packs exist in the connected Core yet.
list.emptyAllBody: Packs appear here after an import completes on the connected Core. This surface never fabricates a pack to fill the list.
list.searchFilterUnavailable: Search and filters are unavailable: the served pack list carries no searchable or facet fields yet, so no search, facet, or sort control is shown (the Core's list is the only view).
list.failureTitle: The pack list could not be loaded
list.failureBody: The Core refused the list read. The code below is the Core's stable machine identifier; the reference is the safe correlation ID for diagnostics.
list.unknownTitle: The pack list could not be confirmed
list.unknownBody: No confirmed response arrived for the list read. Nothing is known about the list until a read is confirmed — this is never shown as an empty list.
list.connectionHint: If no Core session is established yet, connect from the first-run setup with a one-time bootstrap credential.

detail.failureTitle: The pack detail could not be loaded
detail.failureBody: The Core refused the pack read: the pack may not exist for this session, or the read was denied. The code below is the Core's stable machine identifier.
detail.unknownTitle: The pack detail could not be confirmed
detail.unknownBody: No confirmed response arrived for the pack read. Nothing about this pack is known until a read is confirmed.
detail.tabsUnavailableNote: Sources, Claims & evidence, and Provenance stay disabled: the served knowledge family carries no source, claim/evidence, or provenance read yet, so those tabs render no invented content.

overview.title: Title
overview.currentVersionBlock: Current version facts (as the Core reports them)
overview.licenseStatusUnknown: unknown — rendered honestly; this is not a license claim
overview.digest: Pack-root digest (content identity only — never safety, authenticity, or factual truth)

versions.heading: Versions
versions.description: The pack's versions exactly as the Core lists them. Existing versions are immutable: a source-snapshot change creates a new version, it never edits history. Each row opens the canonical immutable-version route.
versions.currentBadge: Current version (as the Core reports it)
versions.empty: The Core reports no versions for this pack yet.
versions.importNewVersionNote: A new version is created through the Core's import operation with this pack as the destination. Prior versions stay visible and immutable.

integrity.heading: Integrity
integrity.description: Integrity facts render only as the Core reports them. A digest establishes content identity relative to the compared bytes only — it never means the content is safe, authentic, factually true, publisher-authorized, or license-compliant. "Verified" appears only when the Core reports a defined verification check and result; no such verification surface is served yet, so no Verified label can appear here.
integrity.digestNote: The algorithm-qualified value form rides the Core's report verbatim; this is a content-identity value, never a truth or safety statement.
integrity.licenseStatusUnknownNote: unknown — rendered as the Core reports it; never a license claim
integrity.signatureTrustNote: No signature, publisher-trust, or verification read is served by the connected Core's knowledge family yet — no such state is displayed, and none is inferred.

export.title: Export knowledge
export.description: The exact scope and destination are confirmed before generation. This is a read-with-output operation on the connected Core.

version.failureTitle: The version could not be loaded
version.failureBody: The Core refused the version read: the version may not exist for this pack, or the read was denied. The code below is the Core's stable machine identifier.
version.unknownTitle: The version could not be confirmed
version.unknownBody: No confirmed response arrived for the version read. Nothing about this version is known until a read is confirmed.
version.heading: Immutable version
version.immutableNote: This version is immutable — Core-enforced. A source-snapshot change creates a new version or an explicit supersession; it never edits old evidence.
version.digestNote: Content identity only — never safety, authenticity, or factual truth.
version.claimsEvidenceNote: The served version read carries no claim or evidence content (the connected Core serves none yet); the counts above are the Core's own report.

import.title: Import source
import.registryFailureBody: The served supported-source registry could not be read, so no source type can be offered: the UI shows only the source types the Core actually serves, and invents none. The code below is the Core's stable machine identifier.
import.registryUnknownBody: No confirmed response arrived for the registry read, so no source type can be offered — nothing is known about the supported list until a read is confirmed.
import.registryHeading: Supported source types (exactly as the Core serves them)
import.registryNoneServed: The Core serves no import source kinds — no speculative format or connector is displayed.
import.kindSizeLimit: The Core's size limit for this kind: {{limit}}
import.fileNameLabel: File (display label only — never a path)
import.sizeAdvisory: Advisory early check only: the file's size against the served limit is client-side feedback and is never a validation result — the Core's validation is authoritative.
import.sizeAdvisoryOver: Advisory only: the locally read size exceeds the served limit for this kind. The Core validates authoritatively and may still refuse.
import.sourceOriginNote: Source origin: the selected file stays on this device until submission; the import request carries the file's bytes to the connected Core.
import.destinationNewPackNote: The import creates a new Core-owned pack identity.
import.destinationExistingPackNote: The import creates a new immutable version under the selected pack.
import.destinationPackEmpty: No packs exist yet — choose "New pack".
import.queueEmpty: No items are queued. Choose files above to queue them.
import.queueRemoveNote: Removing a queued item before submission is a local act: it has no Core meaning, creates no Core event, and needs no confirmation.
import.reviewLimit: The Core's size limit for this kind
import.reviewDestinationNew: New pack (a new Core-owned pack identity)
import.reviewDestinationExisting: Existing pack {{packId}} (a new immutable version under it)
import.reviewOriginValue: This device — the bytes are submitted to the connected Core through the local transport.
import.reviewLicenseFreshnessNone: The served registry carries no license or freshness metadata for this kind — none is shown, none is invented.
import.reviewPermissionValue: The import rides the connected Core's own authorization decision; a UI display is never enforcement.
import.reviewBoundaryValue: The served import kinds read files on the connected local Core's own surface; no provider or remote-Core crossing exists on this surface, so no external-transfer confirmation is required or sent.
import.reviewBoundaryLocalOnly: Nothing crosses to a provider or a remote Core on this surface.
import.reviewUntrustedNote: The submitted bytes are untrusted: the Core validates type, size, schema, archive paths, and policy authoritatively; client checks are early feedback only.
import.submitFailureBody: The Core refused the import submission. The code below is the Core's stable machine identifier.
import.submitUnknownBody: No confirmed response arrived for the submission. This is never proof of success or failure: the outcome is reconciled through the operation ID. The idempotency key for this item was {{idempotencyKey}} — a re-submission with the SAME key and the SAME bytes is safely reconciled by the Core; a different key creates a separate operation.
import.submitConflictSameKey: Same idempotency key, different bytes: the Core reports fingerprintMatch: false. This is a distinct conflict state — recovery is an explicit re-submission with a NEW key, never a silent retry.
import.submitConflictState: The Core refused the operation by state (the replay window or the operation state decides). The code below is the Core's stable machine identifier.

export.title: Export knowledge
export.scopeVersionCurrent: The pack's current version (as the Core reports it)
export.scopeVersionPlaceholder: Select the exact version to export
export.destinationNote: The destination descriptor is shown here before generation and is never assumed. It names where the export is directed on the connected Core's own surface.
export.secretsValue: Secrets are excluded by default — a prohibition, not a preference. No secret value ever enters an export artifact.
export.integrityValue: Integrity is stated only where digest/signature verification was actually performed. The completed result reports the artifact's own digest — that is a content-identity value, never a "verified" label.
export.submitFailureBody: The Core refused the export submission. The code below is the Core's stable machine identifier.
export.submitUnknownBody: No confirmed response arrived for the export submission. This is never proof of success or failure: reconcile through the operation ID before another copy. The correlation ID for this export was {{correlationId}}.

operation.acceptedNote: Accepted for processing (202) — this is never the confirmation: the authoritative state read below confirms the outcome.
operation.noPercentageNote: Progress is the Core's own state/step — never a percentage.
operation.untrustedLabel: Untrusted label (as the Core reports it)
operation.cancelConfirmBody: The cancellation goes to the Core as a request. Post-boundary operations may be non-cancellable — the Core-confirmed state decides. The request is never displayed as the confirmation.
operation.cancelRequestAccepted: The cancellation request was accepted for processing (202). This is not the confirmation — the state read confirms the terminal cancelled state.
operation.cancelRefused: The cancellation was refused. The code below is the Core's stable machine identifier; a terminal operation is non-cancellable by state.
operation.resultNoDownload: The served family carries no artifact download route — the reference and digest above are the Core-confirmed record of the artifact; no download surface is shown, and none is invented.
operation.replayedNote: The Core replayed an existing operation for this identity (replayed) — the reference above is the EXISTING Core-confirmed result, not a newly created one.
operation.completedImportNote: The import completed: the reference above is the Core-created pack-version reference.
operation.completedExportNote: The export completed: the reference and digest above are the Core-confirmed artifact record.
operation.rejectedNote: The import was rejected by the Core's validation — the explicit reason and code below are the Core's own statement. Adjust the submission and resubmit; a resubmission with the SAME key and the SAME bytes is safely reconciled, different bytes need a NEW key.
operation.failedNote: The operation failed inside the Core — the explicit reason and code below are the Core's own statement. Nothing is inferred about the Core's health from one failed operation.
operation.cancelledNote: The Core confirmed the cancellation (the terminal cancelled state) — the operation stopped by the Core's own record.
operation.outcomeUnknownNote: The Core reports outcome_unknown — the outcome is not resolvable right now. Reconcile through this authoritative state read before any retry; a timeout or lost response is never proof of success, cancellation, or safe retry.
operation.reconcileNote: Reconciliation is a pure query by the operation ID — never a retry of the operation itself. Retry controls stay available only after reconciliation resolves the authoritative state.
operation.reconcileFailedBody: The state read itself did not confirm. The explained state stays; no blind retry is performed. Try the reconciliation again — the operation ID above is the reference.
operation.closeDuringLiveNote: Closing now leaves the operation owned by the Core: it continues there, and the resulting pack appears in the library after it completes. This view abandons only the local tracking display.

failure.IMPORT_TYPE_UNSUPPORTED: Unsupported type: the declared source kind or the content's actual type is outside the Core's served registry.
failure.IMPORT_SIZE_OVER_LIMIT: Over limit: the content exceeds the Core's served size bound for this kind.
failure.IMPORT_MALFORMED: Malformed content: the submitted bytes do not form a valid instance of the declared kind.
failure.IMPORT_DUPLICATE_DIGEST: Duplicate digest: the Core reports this content's digest as already imported.
failure.IMPORT_PERMISSION_DENIED: Permission denied: the Core's authorization decision refused this import.
failure.IMPORT_POLICY_BLOCKED: Policy block: the content or an archive entry violates the Core's policy (for example path traversal or symlink rules).
failure.IMPORT_INTEGRITY_SIGNATURE_FAILURE: Integrity/signature failure: the Core's integrity or signature check failed.
failure.IMPORT_NETWORK_INTERRUPTED: Network interruption: the transfer was interrupted — a transient condition.
failure.INTERNAL: Internal failure: the operation failed inside the Core with its own explicit statement.
failure.unknown: The Core reports a failure code this surface does not list; the verbatim code is shown and nothing is inferred beyond it.
failure.recovery: Recovery: adjust the submission per the stated reason and resubmit. A resubmission with the SAME idempotency key and the SAME bytes is safely reconciled by the Core; different bytes require a NEW key.
failure.networkRecovery: Recovery: this is a transient interruption — resubmitting after the connection is restored is the recorded recovery path.
